28th
MARCH
(1) THE COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF SUNDERLAND
-and-
(2)BELLWAY HOMES LIMITED
AGREEMENT
Under Section 106 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990
(as Amended) relating to land on the north side of Burdon Lane, Sunderland
E. Waugh
Assistant Director of Law & Governance
Civic Centre
Sunderland
S2 7DN
Ref: PB/80741
THIS AGREEMENT is made on
28th
March
BETWEEN:
THE COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF SUNDERLAND of Civic Centre, Burdon
Road, Sunderland SR2 7DN ("the Council") and
BELLWAY HOMES LIMITED whose registered address is Woolsington
House, Woolsington, Newcastle Upon Tyne NE13 8BF (Co Regn No
00670176) ("the Developer").
together "the Parties"
WHEREAS
The Council is the Local Planning Authority for the purposes of the Act for the area
within which the Site is located and by whom the obligations contained in this
Agreement are enforceable.
The Developer is the freehold owner of the Site.
The Developer and the Council entered into an Agreement pursuant to S.111
Local Government Act 1972 (as amended) on 18 Fe Javy
The Council's Planning and Highways East Committee resolved to grant Planning
Permission for the Development on 1st November 2021.
The Council and the Developer have agreed to enter into this Agreement with the
intention that the obligations contained in this Agreement may, subject to the
terms of this Agreement, be enforced by the Council against the Developer and
its respective successors in title and any person deriving title from it in relation to
the Site
The Parties have had regard to regulation 122 of the CIL Regulations and consider
that the planning obligations contained in this Agreement are necessary to make
the Development acceptable, are directly related to the Development and are
fairly and reasonably related in scale and kind to the Development.
INTERPRETATION
In this Agreement, the following words and expressions have the following
meanings:
"Act"
the Town and Country Planning Act 1990
(as amended)
"Affordable Housing"
subsidised housing provided to eligible
households whose needs are not met by the
market in accordance with the definition in
Annex 2 of the National Planning Policy
Framework (or any successor policy or
legislation in respect of affordable housing);
"Affordable Housing Units"
Means the 6 (six) Dwellings. to be
constructed on the Site and provided as
Affordable Housing pursuant to the Planning
Permission and identified by a red dot on the
Plan;
"Affordable Rent"
Means the rent payable by individual
households for the Affordable Rented Units
which shall be subject to rent controls that
require a rent of no more than 80 (eighty) per
cent of the local market rent in the vicinity of
the Application Site or such other rent that
may be permitted by the Regulator including
target rents;
"Affordable Rented Units"
Means those five (5) dwellings to be
provided on the Site which are to be owned
and managed by a Registered Provider and
subject at all times to an Affordable Rent.
"Allotments Contribution"
means the contribution of £5580.00 (five
thousand, five hundred and eighty pounds)
to be applied towards the provision and
maintenance of allotments within the Area.
"Area"
the administrative area of the City of
Sunderland
"Biodiversity Contribution"
means the sum of £20,220.00 (twenty
thousand two hundred and twenty pounds)
as a contribution towards biodiversity
enhancements within the Area
"Capital Funding Guide"
the guide published by the Regulator on 4th
November 2016 as updated and amended
and in such form as it may come to be so
updated repealed amended and/or replaced
from time to time.
"Chargee"
any mortgagee or chargee (or any receiver
(including an administrative receiver)
appointed by such mortgagee or chargee or
any other person appointed under any
security documentation to enable such
mortgagee or chargee to realise its security
or any administrator (howsoever appointed)
including a housing administrator (each a
Receiver)) of the whole or any part of the
Affordable Housing Units or the successors
in title to such mortgagee or chargee
"Commencement Date"
the date on which any material operation (as
defined in Section 56(4) of the Act) forming
part of the Development begins to be carried
out other than (for the purposes of this
Agreement and for no other purpose)
operations consisting of environmental
(including ecology) or archaeological
investigations and survey sampling
inspections including soil investigations,
investigations for the purpose of assessing
ground conditions, site survey works,
remedial or mitigation works in respect of
any contamination or other adverse ground
conditions, diversion and laying of services,
demolition works, site clearance (including
works to adjust ground levels on site and the
removal of vegetation), erection of any
temporary means of enclosure, the
temporary display of site notices or
advertisements construction of any
construction access or temporary buildings
and structures and laying out of access
roads and "Commence Development" shall
be construed accordingly
"Development"
The construction of 60 Dwellings and
associated infrastructure on the Site;
"Discounted
Market
Sale the restriction to be entered in the
Restriction"
Proprietorship Register at the Land Registry
in relation to each Discounted Market Unit in
the following terms (but subject to any
amendments thereto required by the Land
Registry and agreed between the relevant
Parties hereto):
"No disposition of the registered estate by
the proprietor of the registered estate or by
the proprietor of any registered charge is to
be registered without a certificate signed by
the solicitor of the disponer or the disponee
that the provisions of paragraphs 12 or 13
(as applicable) of Schedule 4 of the Section
106 Agreement dated 28 Mach2022
and relating to land to the north of Burdon
Lane, Burdon, Sunderland between (1) The
Council of the City of Sunderland and (2)
Bellway Homes Limited have been complied
with or are not relevant to the disposition in
question."
"Discounted Market Unit"
the 1 (one) Affordable Housing Unit which is
to be provided at a Discounted Price in
accordance with Schedule 4.
"Discounted Price"
in the context of respect of the sale of an
Affordable Housing Unit on the open market
means a sale at a discount of thirty percent
(30%) from the Market Value.
"Disposal"
the sale of the freehold or the grant of a
lease of more than 99 (ninety-nine) years
with a ground rent of no more than one
peppercorn per annum but for the avoidance
of doubt reference to 'Disposal' shall not
include the creation of a mortgage or
charge.
"Dwelling"
shall mean any one or more of the dwellings
constructed on the Site pursuant to the
Planning Permission;
"Education Contribution"
means the contribution of £185,700.00 (one
hundred and eighty five thousand seven
hundred pounds) to be applied towards the
provision of a new school within the vicinity
of the Site;
"Eligible Person"
a Qualifying Person (or persons) who meets
the Local Connection Criteria and does not
have a financial interest in any other
property, is not able to resolve their housing
needs on the open market and is in need of
Affordable Housing due to a lack of their own
housing or to living in housing which is
inadequate or unsuitable to meet their
existing and future requirements whether
because of tenure, size, type, design,
condition, security or cost;
"Interest"
means interest at the rate of the Bank of
England base rate from time to time;
"Index"
means the all items index of Retail Prices
issued by the Office for National Statistics
(or any successor organisation) from time to
time;
"Indexation"
means the process specified in clause 21
whereby the amounts payable by the
Developer under the provisions of Schedule
Two to this Agreement are increased in
accordance with any increase in the Index;
"Local Connection"
means a person having a connection with
the Area and as defined in paragraph 8 of
Schedule 4.
"Management Company"
means a limited UK company which may
already be in existence or which may be
formed by the Developer and whose primary
objects include and permit it to carry out the
future management and maintenance of the
Privately Maintained Areas (or any part
thereof) whether or not including
management and maintenance of aspects
of the Development.
"Management Plan"
the detailed specification and plan for the
management and maintenance of the
Privately Maintained Areas, including
(without prejudice to the generality)
maintenance, repair, renewal and cleaning
of such areas including all landscaping,
street furniture, security equipment,
drainage, signage and information displays,
lighting and all other facilities in relation to
any Privately Maintained Areas, which
Management Plan shall also identify the
extent of those Privately Maintained Areas
located within the Phase to which it relates
and which is to be submitted to and
approved by the Council in accordance with
Schedule 3 to this Agreement.
"Market Housing Units"
those Dwellings to be provided on the Site
as part of the Development which are
general market housing for sale on the open
market and not Affordable Housing
"Marketing Period"
means a period of twelve (12) months from
receipt by a Registered Provider of
documentation for the Affordable Housing
Units;
"Market Value"
a figure representing the estimated amount
for which the Discounted Market Unit should
exchange on the date of valuation on the
open market free from the restrictions in the
Deed between a willing buyer and a willing
seller in an arm's length transaction after
proper marketing wherein the parties had
each acted knowledgeably, prudently and
without compulsion such value to be
assessed (other than in relation to the first
sale of any Discounted Market Unit) in
accordance with the Practice Statement of
the Sixth Edition of the RICS Valuation
Standards (as amended).;
"National Planning Policy
the government planning policy document
Framework"
published by the Department for
Communities and Local Government dated
July 2021 and as amended from time to time
and "NPPF" shall be construed accordingly;
"Occupation" and "Occupied" occupation for the purposes permitted by
the Planning Permission but not including
occupation by personnel engaged in
construction, fitting out or decoration or
occupation for marketing or display or
occupation in relation to security operations
only or as site office
"Offer Period"
a period of six (6) months from receipt of
offer documentation for the Affordable
Housing Units to be provided in the relevant
Sub-Phase by a Registered Provider.
"Open Spaces Plan"
the plans attached to this Agreement and
(showing the open space areas)
"Permitted Closures"
temporary closure of the privately
Maintained Areas or the SANG or any part
thereof in the following circumstances:
except for the SANG Areas closure
for a maximum of 1 (one) day. per
year to assert rights of proprietorship
preventing public rights from coming
into being by means of prescription or
other process of law (provided that
for the avoidance of this shall not
prevent the erection of appropriate
signage to prevent (or to evidence an
intention to prevent) any such public
rights arising);
in the case of emergency a
temporary closure where such
closure is necessary in the interest of
public safety or otherwise for reasons
of public safety;
in accordance with any lawful
requirement of the police or any other
competent body;
with the prior approval of the Council
where the Council is satisfied (acting
reasonably) that such temporary
closure is necessary for the purposes
of maintenance repair cleansing
renewal or resurfacing works within
the Privately Maintained Area or
SANG (or, in each case, part thereof)
or for any other reasonable kand
proper purpose; and
with the prior approval of the Council
where the Council is satisfied (acting
reasonably) that such temporary closure is
necessary for the purpose of carrying out
worksof
construction
(including
development or redevelopment or for the
placing or replacing of underground
services) within either of the Developments.
"Plan"
the plan attached to this Agreement and
marked "390-BEL-100Q Site Plan" (showing
the Site and the Affordable Housing Units)
"Planning Application"
the planning application for the
Development validated on 1st July 2021 and
allocated the reference 21/01544/FU4
"Planning Permission"
the full planning permission granted in
pursuance of the Planning Application (and
for the purposes of this Agreement including
any new or varied planning permission that
may be granted on an application pursuant
to Section 73 of the Act relating to, and or in
connection with, the Planning Permission);
"Practical Completion"
the issue of a certificate of practical
completion by the Developer's architect or in
the event that the Development is
constructed by a party other than the
Developer the issue of a certificate of
practical completion by that other party's
architect confirming that the relevant
Housing Units are practically complete;
"Privately Maintained Areas"
means the following areas:
the areas identified on the Open
Spaces Plan;
un-adopted roads (but excluding
private drives and access-ways); and
any
un-adopted
multi-user
routes/path links, informal play
areas and communal amenity
spaces outside the SANG Area
(which is to be provided and
maintained as required by Schedule
"Protected Tenant"
any tenant who:
Has exercised the right to acquire pursuant
to the Housing Act 1996 or any statutory
provision for the time being in force (or any
equivalent contractual right) in respect of a
particular Affordable Housing Unit;
Has exercised any statutory right to buy (or
any equivalent contractual right) in respect
of a particular Affordable Housing Unit;
Has been granted a Shared Ownership
Lease by a Registered Provider (or similar
arrangement where a share of the
Affordable Housing Unit is owned by the
tenant and a share is owned by the
Registered Provider) in respect of a
particular Affordable Housing Unit and the
tenant has subsequently purchased from
the Registered Provider all remaining
shares so that the tenant owns the entire
Affordable Housing Unit;
Public Transport
means the sum of £20,580.00 (twenty
Contribution"
thousand five hundred and eighty pounds)
as a contribution towards the cost of pump
priming a bus service for the site for a period
of 12 (twelve) years.
"Qualifying Person"
a person who qualifies for the purposes of
the applicant eligibility set out in paragraph
1.4 of Chapter 2 of the Capital Funding
Guide or any replacement provisions
relating to Rent to Buy Units
"RDLR Contribution"
means the contribution of £120,120.00 (one
hundred and twenty thousand one hundred
and twenty pounds) towards the design,
construction and maintenance of the
Ryhope Doxford Park Link Road
"Recreation Contribution"
means the contribution of £55,620.00 (fifty
five thousand, six hundred and twenty
pounds) to be invested in play facilities in the
Area.
"Registered Provider"
means a registered provider of social
housing as defined in Section 80 of the
Housing and Regeneration Act 2008 who is
registered with the Homes and Communities
Agency as required pursuant to section 111
of that Act and has not been removed from
the register pursuant to Section 118 or 119
of that Act
"Regulator"
means the Regulator of Social Housing
established pursuant to Part 2 of the
Housing and Regeneration Act 2008 trading
as Homes England or any similar authority
(including any statutory successor) carrying
on substantially the same regulatory or
supervisory functions;
"SANG Area"
those areas of the Site identified and marked
on the SANG Plan as 'SANG Area' and
including for the avoidance of doubt any
routes therein identified as 'multi-user
route/path links' to be provided in the SANG
Area in accordance with the SANG
Specification and the provisions of Schedule
3 and 6 to this Agreement and the term
SANG shall include any part thereof.
"SANG Area Commuted Sum"
means the contribution of £105,000.00 (one
hundred and five thousand pounds) towards
the continued maintenance of the SANG
Areas in accordance with the SANG
Specification by the Council;
"SANG Plan"
the drawing numbered 001 Rev. P01
and attached to this Agreement at Appendix
"SANG Specification"
the detailed specification for the design,
construction and subsequent management
and maintenance of the SANG as part of the
Development which shall be in accordance
with the Design Code within Chapter 9 of the
South
Sunderland
Growth
Area
Supplementary Planning Document dated
June 2020.
"Site"
the land described in Schedule 1 and
against which this Agreement may be
enforced as shown edged red on the Plan
(and including any part thereof);
"Working Days"
Monday to Friday inclusive but excluding
weekends and any public holiday in
England.
The expression "the Developer" shall include its respective successors in title
and assigns and any person deriving title to the Site through or under it
The expression "the Council" shall include any statutory successor to its function
as the Local Planning Authority
References to the "Site" and the "Development" include any part of it
Words importing one gender shall be construed as importing any gender and
words importing the singular shall be construed as importing the plural and words
importing persons include companies and corporations and vice versa
Where in this Agreement reference is made to any clause, paragraph or
schedule or recital such reference (unless the context otherwise requires) is a
reference to a clause, paragraph or schedule or recital in this Agreement
Whenever there is more than one person named as a party and where more
than one party undertakes an obligation all their obligations can be enforced
against all of them jointly or severally unless there is an express provision
otherwise.
Any reference to an Act of Parliament shall include any modification, extension
or re-enactment of that Act for the time being in force and shall include all
instruments, orders, plans, regulations, permissions and directions for the time
being made, issued or given under that Act or deriving validity from it.
Any covenant contained in this Agreement whereby a party is not to do any act
or thing includes a covenant not to permit or allow the doing of that act or thing.
1.10 References in this Agreement to the term "including" shall be construed as
meaning "including without limitation".
The headings are for reference only and shall not affect construction.
LEGAL BASIS
This Agreement is made pursuant to Section 106 of the Act, Section 111 of the
Local Government Act 1972, Section 1 of the Localism Act 2011 and all other
enabling powers on behalf of the Council.
The covenants, restrictions and requirements imposed upon the Developer
under this Agreement create planning obligations pursuant to Section 106 of the
Act in respect of the Site and are enforceable by the Council as local planning
authority against the Developer.
CONDITIONALITY
Save as provided in clause 3.2 the obligations contained in this Agreement are
conditional upon:-
3.1.1 the grant of the Planning Permission; and
3.1.2the Commencement of Development.
The provisions of clauses 6.1, 14, 15, 18 and 19 shall take effect on the date of
this Agreement
The obligations contained in this Agreement will not be enforceable against:
3.3.1 the owners, occupiers or tenants of an individual Dwelling erected on the
Site pursuant to the Planning Permission nor against their Chargees or
those deriving title from them save that the obligations contained in
Schedules 4 and 5 shall be enforceable against the owner/occupier of an
Affordable Housing Unit; or
3.3.2 a statutory undertaker after the transfer of the statutory apparatus and
any land upon or in which the statutory apparatus is situated by the
Developer to that statutory undertaker.
THE DEVELOPER'S COVENANTS
The Developer covenants with the Council to fully observe and perform the
obligations in this Agreement including those obligations set out in Schedules 2,
4, 5, 6 and 7 and hereby agrees that the Site shall be subject to the obligations,
restrictions and covenants herein, such obligations being planning obligations
for the purposes of Section 106 of the Act.
THE COUNCIL'S COVENANTS
The Council covenants with the Developer to observe and perform the
obligations on its part in this Agreement including those obligations set out in
Schedule 3.
THE COUNCIL'S FEES
The Developer shall pay to the Council on completion of this Agreement the sum
of £850.00 (eight hundred and fifty pounds) in respect of the Council's legal costs
incurred in the preparation and completion of this Agreement.
The Developer covenants to pay to the Council on the grant of Planning
Permission a monitoring fee of £8,750.00 (eight thousand seven hundred and
fifty pounds) as a contribution towards the expenses incurred by the Council in
monitoring, reporting and ensuring compliance with the obligations on the part
of the Developer comprised in this Agreement.
LOCAL LAND CHARGE
This Agreement shall be registrable as a local land charge by the Council
The Council shall upon written request of the Developer at any time after either:
7.2.1 all of the obligations of the Developer under this Agreement have been
discharged in full; or
7.2.2 this Agreement has been terminated pursuant to Clause 9
issue written confirmation thereof and thereafter shall effect the cancellation of
all entries in the Local Land Charges Register in respect of this Agreement.
COUNCIL'S CONSENT ETC AND NOTICES
Where the agreement, approval, consent or expression of satisfaction is required
by the Developer from the Council under the terms of this Agreement such
agreement, approval or consent or expression of satisfaction shall not be
unreasonably withheld or delayed and any such agreement, consent, approval
or expression of satisfaction shall be given on behalf of the Council by the
Executive Director of City Development (or such other person as notified by the
Council to the Developer from time to time) and any notices shall be deemed to
have been properly served if sent by recorded delivery to the principal address
or registered office (as appropriate) of the relevant party.
TERMINATION
This Agreement shall cease to have effect (insofar only as it has not already
been complied with) if the Planning Permission shall be quashed, revoked or
otherwise withdrawn or (without the consent of the Developer) it is modified by
any statutory procedure or expires prior to the Commencement Date.
THIRD PARTIES
Save to the extent expressly provided otherwise in this Agreement, no provisions
of this Agreement shall be enforceable under the Contracts (Rights of Third
Parties) Act 1999.
LIABILITY
No person shall be liable for any breach, non-performance and non-observance
of any covenant, obligation or restriction or other provision of this Agreement
after it shall have parted with its entire interest in the Site or that part to which
such breach relates but without prejudice to liability for any subsisting breach
arising prior to parting with such interest.
STATUTORY POWERS
Nothing contained or implied in this Agreement shall prejudice or affect the rights
discretions powers duties and obligations of the Council under all statutes by-
laws statutory instruments orders and regulations in the exercise of its functions
as a local authority and local planning authority.
SEVERANCE
Insofar as any provision of this Agreement is found (for whatever reason) to be
invalid illegal or unenforceable then such invalidity illegality or unenforceability
shall not affect the validity or enforceability of the remaining provisions of this
Agreement.
WAIVER
No waiver (whether expressed or implied) by any party of any breach or default
in performing or observing any of the covenants terms or conditions of this
Agreement shall constitute a continuing waiver and no such waiver shall prevent
any party from enforcing any of the relevant terms or conditions or from acting
upon any subsequent breach or default.
CHANGE IN OWNERSHIP
Until the covenants and restrictions in this Agreement including those obligations
set out in the Schedule 2 have been discharged in full, the Developer agrees
with the Council to give the Council immediate written notice of any change in
ownership of its. interest in the Site occurring before all of the obligations in this
Agreement. have been discharged such notice to give details of the transferee's
full name and registered office or correspondence address together with the area
of the Site transferred by reference to a plan SAVE THAT this clause shall not
apply in respect of the sale of an individual Dwelling.
DISPUTE RESOLUTION
In the event of any dispute or difference arising between any of the parties to
this Deed in respect of any matter contained in this Deed such dispute or
difference shall be referred to an independent and suitable person holding
appropriate professional qualifications to be appointed (in the absence of an
agreement) by or on behalf of the president for the time being of the professional
body chiefly relevant in England with such matters as may be in dispute and
such person shall act as an expert whose decision shall be final and binding on
the parties in the absence of manifest error and any costs shall be payable by
the parties to the dispute in such proportion as the expert shall determine and
failing such determination shall be borne by the Developer.
In the absence of agreement as to the appointment or suitability of the person to
be appointed pursuant to clause 16.1 or as to the appropriateness of the
professional body then such question may be referred by either party to the
president for the time being of the Law Society for him to appoint a solicitor to
determine the dispute such solicitor acting as an expert and his decision shall
be final and binding on all parties in the absence of manifest error and his costs
shall be payable by the parties to the dispute in such proportion as he shall
determine and failing such determination shall be borne by the Developer.
Any expert howsoever appointed shall be subject to the express requirement
that a decision was reached and communicated to the relevant parties within the
minimum practicable timescale allowing for the nature and complexity of the
dispute and in any event not more than twenty-eight working days after the
conclusion of any hearing that takes place or twenty-eight working days after he
has received any file or written representation.
The expert shall be required to give notice to each of the said parties requiring
them to submit to him within ten working days of notification of his appointment
written submissions and supporting material and the other party will be entitled
to make a counter written submission within a further ten working days.
16.5 This clause 16 does not apply to disputes in relation to matters of law or the
construction or interpretation of any provision of this Deed or to the recovery of
sums due under this Deed which will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of
the Courts and further does not affect the ability of the Council to apply for or to
be granted declaratory relief, an injunction, an order for specific performance,
payment of any sum and any other means of enforcing this Agreement and
consequential and interim orders and relief.
INTEREST
If any payment (including any part thereof) due under this Agreement is paid late,
Interest shall be payable by the party in default which shall accrue at an annual
rate from the date the payment is due until the actual date of payment.
JURISDICTION
This Agreement shall be governed by and interpreted in accordance with the law
of England and the parties submit to the exclusive jurisdiction of the English
courts.
FUTURE PLANNING PERMISSIONS
Nothing in this Agreement shall prohibit or limit the right to develop any part of
the Site in accordance with any planning permission (other than the Planning
Permission or modification, variation or amendment thereof) granted after the
date of the Planning Permission whether or not on appeal.
NOTICES
Any notice, demand or any other communication served under this Agreement
will be effective only if delivered by hand or sent by first class post, pre-paid or
recorded delivery.
Any notice, demand or any other communication served is to be sent to the
Council at the address set out at the beginning of this Deed or to such other
address as one party may notify in writing to the others at any time as its address
for service.
3 Unless the time of actual receipt is proved, a notice, demand or communication
sent by the following means is to be treated as having been served:-
20.3.1 if delivered by hand or by fax or e-mail, at the time of delivery;
20.3.2 if sent by first class post on the second working day after posting;
20.3.3 if sent by recorded delivery, at the time the delivery was signed for.
INDEXATION
The sum payable under the provisions of Schedule Two to this Agreement shall
be increased by an amount equivalent to the increase in the Index from the date
of this Agreement until the date on which each sum is payable using the following
formula increased in accordance with the following formula:
Amount payable =
the payment specified in this deed x (A/B) where:
A=
the figure for the Index that applied immediately
preceding the date of payment
B=
the figure for the Index that applied when the index
was last published prior to the date of this deed.
Where reference is made to an Index and that index ceases to exist or is
replaced or rebased then it shall include reference to any index which replaces
it or any rebased index (applied in a fair and reasonable manner to the periods
before and after rebasing under this deed) or in the event the index is not
replaced, to an alternative reasonably comparable basis or index as the Council
shall advise the Developer in writing.
IN WITNESS whereof this Agreement has been duly executed as a Deed by the parties
hereto the day and year first before written

six (6) of the Affordable Housing Units are ready for Occupation.

Development as approved in writing and in advance by the Council and shall

all responses and representations received from Registered Providers during the

those matters set out in Paragraph 6 below; and

the number of Affordable Housing Units that need to be provided within the

The Affordable Rented Units shall be allocated in accordance with the procedure
in Schedule 5.
The Discount Market Unit shall not be used other than as for Affordable Housing
by an Eligible Person who meets at least one of the following Local Connection
criteria (the applicant to purchase such Unit to satisfy and evidence one or more
of such criteria) so that the applicant:
must currently live in the Area and have done so for the last 12 (twelve)
months;
must be employed on a permanent basis within the Area or have retired
from employment within the Area and wish to remain in the Area (priority
will be given to key workers who fill a skills shortage in the Area);
must have a long standing family connection to the Area, such as the

In the event that an Eligible Person who meets at least one of the Local

months the Discount Market Units can be sold to a person who does not meet
the Local Connection criteria.
The Discounted Market Unit shall not be available to investors on a buy to let
basis.
The Discounted Market Units shall not be sold other than in accordance with the
process for re-sales (set out in Paragraph 13 below) below and to an Eligible

Prior to first Disposal of the Discounted Market Unit:
12.1.1 the Developer will serve a Sunderland City Council Application Form
and evidence of eligibility on the Council addressed to the Council's

the Council will notify the Developer within 10 (ten) Working Days after

12.1.3 the Discounted Market Unit shall not be Disposed of other than In

the existing registered owner of the Unit will notify the Council of such

the existing registered owner will market the Dwelling (including advising

SCHEDULE 5
Affordable Housing Allocations Procedure
The Registered Provider and the Council shall each nominate a contact person
for the purposes of administering the allocation procedures for the Affordable
Rented Units and shall notify the other of the name and contact details of that
person.
The Registered Provider will:
in respect of Initial Lettings provide the Council with at least 3 (three)
weeks written notification of when it intends to commence marketing of
the Affordable Rented Units and in the case of the initial letting of the
Affordable Rented Unit shall not give notification unless in the
reasonable opinion of the Developer the Affordable Rented Unit will be
Practically Completed and available for Occupation within eight (8)
weeks; and
provide the Council with a schedule of the Affordable Rented Units
confirming the rent to be charged.
Within 8 (eight) weeks of receiving the above information, the Council will provide
the Registered Provider with a list of prospective tenants drawn from the
Council's housing register. The list will rank each prospective tenant in terms of
their priority housing need and the type of property that meets their housing
requirements subject to the Council providing no more than 3 (three) referrals to
the Registered Provider for each Affordable Rented Unit on any one occasion.
The Registered Provider will write to all parties referred by the Council providing
details of the Affordable Rented Units available and asking them to inform their
nominated contact person if they are interested in renting one of the Affordable
rented Units.
The Affordable Rented Units will be allocated in the priority need order to those
prospective tenants that:
confirm to the Registered Provider their interest in rented an Affordable
Rented Unit; and
are successfully financially qualified as being in a position to rent.
In the event that:
insufficient tenants are referred by the Council; or
those that are referred do not confirm their interest in renting within 4
(four) weeks of being contacted by the Registered Provider; or
a person having confirmed their interest within the time specified in
Paragraph 6.1.2 has failed to be financially qualified as required by
Paragraph 5.1.2 within a further period of 4 (four) weeks; or
a person having confirmed their interest within the time specified in
Paragraph 6.1.2 and having been shown to be financially qualified within
the said further period of 4 (four) weeks has failed to sign. a tenancy
agreement within a further period of 8 (eight) weeks; and
once all the persons who have confirmed their interest within the time
period specified in Paragraph 6.1.2 and have been financially qualified
in accordance with the time period set out in Paragraph 6.1.3 but have
failed to sign a tenancy agreement in accordance with the time period
set out in Paragraph 6.1.4, the Registered Provider may allocate any
available properties to persons whom in its opinion are not able to
resolve their housing needs on the open market and have responded to
local press advertising of the Affordable Rented Units, but priority shall
be given to:
(a)persons currently residing in the Area or who used to reside in the
Area but had to move away in order to secure appropriate
accommodation;
(persons working or residing in the Area;
persons working or residing in the North East Region.
The Registered Provider shall provide a monthly update to the Council regarding
the allocation of the Affordable Rented Units which will include details as to whom
the properties were offered to, the response received, whether the party was
successfully financially qualified and to whom the property has been allocated.
The update provided by the Registered Provider pursuant to Paragraph 7 will
also include the total number of applications received, financial, age and
professional profiling of all applicants in addition to their housing status prior to
renting or applying to rent an Affordable Rented Unit.
For the avoidance of doubt, nothing in this Schedule shall require the processing
or disclosure of data in contravention or potential contravention of the Data
Protection Act 2018.
SCHEDULE 6
The Privately Maintained Areas and SANG Area(s)
Part 1
Provision of the SANG Areas
The SANG Area shall be a minimum of 1.08 hectares as shown on the SANG
Plan.
Part 2
Provision of the Privately Maintained Areas
The Developer shall:
Provide the Privately Maintained Areas in accordance with the Open Spaces
Plan as approved by the Council and the provisions of this Schedule 6 to the
reasonable satisfaction of the Council;
Practically Complete the whole of the Privately Maintained Areas prior to
Occupation of the final Dwelling;
Following. Practical Completion of the Privately Maintained Areas (including any
part thereof) maintain such open Space Area(s) in perpetuity for the purposes of
public recreation and as amenity land to the reasonable satisfaction of the
Council;
neither use, nor permit to be used, the Privately Maintained Areas at any time for
any purpose other than for public recreation and as amenity land; and
provide public access at all times to and across the Privately Maintained Areas.
At any time following completion of any Privately Maintained Areas (or part
thereof), the Developer shall be at liberty to transfer such Privately Maintained
Areas (or part thereof) to a Management Company (provided that before doing
so the Developer shall first supply to the Council a certified copy of the
Memorandum and Articles of Association of the Management Company) and
upon completion of such transfer, the obligations in this Schedule relating to the
UI
Privately Maintained Areas (or part thereof) so transferred shall thereafter be
performed by the Management Company.
SCHEDULE 7
The Management Plan
The Developer shall produce a Management Plan in respect of the management
and maintenance of the Privately Maintained Areas in accordance with the
provisions of this Schedule 7 and for subsequent approval by the Council.
The Developer shall:
not Occupy any Dwelling until the Management Plan has been submitted to and
approved in writing by the Council; and
implement and comply at all times with the requirements of the Management
Plan in respect of the Privately Maintained Areas to the satisfaction of the
Council.
As a minimum, the Management Plan shall identify the extent of those Privately
Maintained Areas located within the respective Phase and cover all of the
following items:
details of regular street sweeping within the Privately Maintained Areas;
details of how the roads, footways and footpaths within the Development
will be maintained and repaired at all times;
details of how car parking on street within the Development will be
managed at all times;
details of general bin emptying;
fly tipping or excess waste removal;
snow clearing and gritting;
maintenance and repair of hard landscaped areas;
maintenance and clearance of gullies;
provision and maintenance of street lighting (including energy charges)
for standard columns and low height lighting units;
details of how pedestrian/cycle routes through the site will be kept safe
for pedestrian/cycle use and how they will be maintained;
street weed control;
maintenance of soft landscaping areas including weeding, watering,
fertilizing, replacement of failures, trimming and pruning of trees and
shrubs, grass cutting, removal and replacement of seriously damaged,
diseased or dead trees and maintenance of water features;
provision and maintenance of signage for pedestrian/cycle routes;
provision of road markings (e.g. "Give way" "Passing Place" etc) and
regular refreshment of these markings;
seasonal maintenance (e.g. leaf clearance);
provision and maintenance of street furniture, seats, liter bins and
bollards;
provision and maintenance of street name plates;
a tree management plan for any trees adjacent to these walls and/or
overhanging the adopted highway;
reinstatement of private utility apparatus trenches to the original palette
materials after essential works;
annual inspections of highways and structures for maintenance purposes;
and
any other information in relation to the management, maintenance and/or
repair of the Privately Maintained Areas as may be required by the
Council (acting reasonably).
Each Management Plan shall not be amended without the prior written consent
of the Council.
Subject to Paragraph 5 of this Schedule 7, following completion of the Privately
Maintained Areas within each Phase the Developer shall maintain the Privately
Maintained Areas in that Phase in perpetuity and in full accordance with the
Management Plan for that Phase and shall provide and maintain at all times
public access to the Privately Maintained Areas in that Phase SUBJECT
ALWAYS to Permitted Closures.
At any time following completion of any Privately Maintained Area (or part
thereof), the Developer shall be at liberty to transfer such Privately Maintained
Area (or part thereof) to a Management Company (provided that before doing so
the Developer shall first supply to the Council a certified copy of the
Memorandum and Articles of Association of the Management Company) and
upon completion of such transfer, the obligations in this Schedule relating to the
Privately Maintained Area(s) (or part thereof) so transferred shall thereafter be
performed by the Management Company.
Nothing in this Schedule 7 shall prevent the Council in its discretion (and in
agreement with the Developer):
adopting any part(s) of the Privately Maintained Areas as public highway
maintainable at the public expense (where the same may be capable of adoption
pursuant to the provisions of the Highways Act 1980); or
taking a transfer of any part(s) of the Privately Maintained Areas and/or otherwise
entering into an agreement with the Developer pursuant to the Open Spaces Act
1906 pursuant to which the Council assumes responsibility for the maintenance,
management and control of such Privately Maintained Areas (or part thereof as
the case may be)
and upon adoption of such part(s) of the Privately Maintained Areas as public
highway or completion of any transfer or agreement as is referred to in
Paragraph 6.2, the provisions of this Schedule 7 shall cease to apply to such
part(s) of the Privately Maintained Areas as may be adopted or transferred or
subject to an agreement as referred to in Paragraph 6.2.
